day_local: Arnaqutaa Tallimanik Aippaa (Saturday) in the 24th Week of Ordinary Time
greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the peace of Christ, who is the resurrection and the life, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the seed that fell to earth to bring forth eternal life: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the first fruits of those who have fallen asleep: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you call us to walk in the light of your presence: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: I will walk in the presence of God, in the light of the living.
homily:
We often look at the world as if it were a finished product, a static landscape that stays exactly as it is. We see the pavement, the concrete, the walls of our homes, and we assume these things define the boundaries of our reality. But today, the Apostle Paul invites us to look deeper, to see beneath the surface of what we call 'natural' and recognize the hidden, spiritual architecture of God's design. Paul uses the image of a seed—a simple, bare kernel of wheat. He tells us that what we sow is not the body that is to be. It must die to its current form so that it can be raised into something glorious, something powerful, something that belongs not just to the earth, but to the heavens.

Think of that seed. It is small, seemingly insignificant, and yet it carries within it a secret, a promise of a harvest that is beyond our current ability to imagine. This is the truth of our existence. We are not merely creatures of the dust, though we bear the image of the earthly. We are being prepared, through every joy and every sorrow, to bear the image of the heavenly. This is the great mystery of our faith: that death is not the end of the story, but the breaking open of the husk so that the true life can emerge.

I think of Benjamin. I think of that quiet, brilliant boy who looked at the world with such wonder—a boy who could see the logic of a complex system just as easily as he could see the beauty in a flight path. Benjamin was a boy who understood that life is meant to be lived with curiosity and with an open heart. He was like that good soil in the Gospel, the heart that hears the word and embraces it with generosity. You remember the way he would talk about his dreams, about the things he wanted to build, the way he would smile when he spoke of his 'Con Chim Airlines'. That joy, that creative fire, was the fruit of a spirit that was already leaning toward the light.

There is a profound comfort in knowing that the life Benjamin lived was not a flicker that simply went out, but a seed that has been planted in the garden of God. When we speak of him, we are not speaking of someone who is absent; we are speaking of someone who has been transformed. Paul tells us that what is sown is corruptible, but what is raised is incorruptible. Benjamin’s kindness, his empathy, the way he offered his entire piggy bank to help his uncle—those were not just fleeting actions. They were signs of a soul that was already participating in the life of the Kingdom. That generosity, that desire to give everything he had to help another, is the signature of a heart that is truly alive in Christ.

I want to speak to you, Alan and Thao, and to you, Ryan. I know that the world feels different now. I know that the silence in the house is a presence of its own. But remember that the seed does not know the glory of the wheat until it has surrendered its shell. Your love for Benjamin, and his love for you, is the soil in which his life continues to grow. You have not lost him. You have simply entrusted him to the One who is the Lord of the harvest. The bond you share is not broken by the veil of death; it is only hidden for a time, just as the life of the seed is hidden in the dark earth before it springs forth into the light.

Do not let the weight of your grief make you doubt the goodness of God. Sometimes we wonder if we could have done more, if we could have protected him better, if we could have held on tighter. But these are the questions of the earthly man, the man who lives by the logic of the world. The heavenly man, the one who walks in the light of the living, knows that God is the Sower, and His hand is gentle. He does not waste a single life. He does not overlook a single tear. He gathers everything—every giggle, every dream of an airplane, every act of quiet mercy—and He weaves it into the tapestry of His eternal Kingdom.

Ryan, you are his brother, his best friend. You know the way Ben looked at the world. You know the things that made him laugh. Carry that with you. When you look at the sky, when you see a plane climbing, when you work on a project that excites your mind, know that you are carrying the legacy of his spirit. You are the witness to his life. Do not be afraid to be happy, to pursue your own dreams, to build your own future. Ben would want that for you. He would want you to soar. He is cheering you on, not from a distance, but from the heart of the Father, where all things are made new.

To all of you who feel the ache of a loss that seems too heavy to bear: you are not alone. The Gospel today warns us of the thorns—the anxieties and the riches and the pleasures of life that can choke the word of God. But the promise of the Resurrection is stronger than any thorn. It is the promise that the seed will bear fruit a hundredfold. Your sorrow, if you bring it to Jesus, will not be the end of you. It will be the place where your faith takes root. It will be the place where you learn to trust, not in your own strength, but in the power of the One who raised Jesus from the dead.

We are all, in a sense, like the seed. We are waiting for our own transformation. We are waiting for the moment when we, too, will be raised in glory. Until then, we walk by faith. We walk in the presence of God. We fulfill our vows, we offer our thank offerings, and we keep our eyes fixed on the light of the living. Benjamin is already there, in that light. He is waiting for us at the Banquet. He is safe, he is whole, and he is loved.

What can you carry out the door today? It is a small, quiet action. When you feel the weight of the day, stop and take a deep breath. Look up. Acknowledge that the sky you see is the same sky that Benjamin is now experiencing in the fullness of God’s glory. Whisper his name, not as a cry of pain, but as a prayer of connection. And then, trust that you are held. You are held by the same God who calls the seed to life. You are held by the same love that Benjamin is currently enjoying. You are part of a family that stretches from this earth into the very heart of heaven. Go in peace, knowing that you are never alone, and that the love you have given is the seed of a harvest that will never end.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you in His light, and may the peace of Christ dwell in your hearts forever. Amen.
standing_petitions: For Benjamin Vo and all who have gone before us, that they may rest in the eternal light of Christ's presence.
For all who carry the cross of grief, that God may console them with the hope of the resurrection and the peace of His love.

readings.label: Atuagak 1
readings.text: Qatanngutikka: Kina uqaqtauliqpa, 'Tuqungajut makititaulirniaqpat? Qanuittuuvvut timiqaqhutik utirniaqpat?' Ilisaijijut! Pijaujuq nunamut pitaujuq inuulirniaqpa, tuqunganngippat. Ammalu pijaujuq timiunngittuq, kisiani ippik, imalunnit avatittinni. Taanna makititauninga tuqungajunit. Pijaujuq akuliqutauluni, makititauluni qaumajumik. Pijaujuq kinguvauluni, makititauluni ujjirnartumik. Pijaujuq sannginngittumik, makititauluni sanngijumik. Pijaujuq timiinnarmik, makititauluni timiqaqtuq isumanginnik. Taanna siulirijaujuq timi, taanna isumanginnik timi. Taanna siulirijaujuq, Adam, inuulaurpuq, ammalu kingulliq Adam inuulirijumik anirniq. Kisiani anirniq siulirijaujuq, ammalu timi. Siulirijaujuq nunamit, nunamiutaujuq; aippaa nunamit, qilammiutaujuq. Qanuittuuvvut nunamiutaujuq, taakkua nunamiutaujut, ammalu qanuittuuvvut qilammiutaujuq, taakkua qilammiutaujut. Qanuittumik tigumiaqtaujuta nunamiutaujumik, tigumiaqtaulirniaqpuq qilammiutaujumik.

readings.label: Tusaajaujuq Psalm
readings.text: R. I will walk in the presence of God, in the light of the living. Qaujimavunga Ataniq uigulirniarmat. Ataniq, angiqtaujumi uqalaurpunga, Ataniq upalungaijarpunga; kina uqumaittumik pijunnarpa? R. I will walk in the presence of God, in the light of the living. Ataniq, angiqtaujunga, uqausiit malikpaka. Anirniq tuqunganit aniguijauvunga, ammalu isigakka tuqunganit; taanna inuulirniaqpuq Ataniup qaumanirni. R. I will walk in the presence of God, in the light of the living.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: Inuit katutillugit, Jiisusi uqausimik uqaqpuq. 'Inuit nunamut tunisijut. Ilanga nunamut, ammalu tingmiat nirijut. Ilanga ujaqqamut, ammalu qaujimajaujuq. Ilanga qijungnut, ammalu qijungnut qipilaurpuq. Ilanga nunami, ammalu inuulirpuq.' Jiisusi uqausimik uqaqpuq, 'Kina tusaajunnarpat, tusarluni.' Jiisusiup nuliangit tusaajumallutik. Jiisusi uqaqpuq, 'Ilissi qaujimajusi qilammiutaujut, kisiani inuit parables-kunni. Taanna tusaajaujuq: taanna uqausiq God-mit. Taakkua nunami, tusaajut, kisiani Devil-up tigujaujuq. Taakkua ujaqqami, tusaajut, kisiani sannginngittut. Taakkua qijungni, tusaajut, kisiani uqumaittunik. Taakkua nunami, tusaajut ammalu inuulirniaqtut.'

day: Saturday of the Twenty-fourth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.

Ben ơi, ba nhớ con nhiều quá.

Mommy cũng vậy. Hơn hai tháng rồi mà ba má vẫn khóc mỗi ngày.

Con giúp ba má vượt qua nha, để lo cho em
Hey Ben,  nếu có thể hãy cho anh Minh gặp Ben trong giấc mơ nhé, dù chỉ là lời chào hay nụ cười như cách Ben vẫn hay tạo dáng để chụp hình. Nhớ và thương Ben nhiều lắm
